rationale: The hypothesis posits a strict rule: biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function (LoF) or null variants invariably spare the anterior temporal lobes, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants reliably cause classic anterior temporal pole hyperintensities resembling CADASIL. Large systematic series such as Iruzubieta et al. (2024) and case studies by Tasharrofi et al. (2024) show a clear divergence where biallelic LoF variants primarily manifest as an early-onset pediatric neurodevelopmental disorder with periventricular/periatrial white matter volume loss and spared anterior temporal poles, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants preserve the adult-onset CADASIL spectrum (with typical temporal pole and external capsule leukoencephalopathy). However, the absolute claim ('strictly dictated') is challenged by recent reports such as Ouskri et al. (2025), which report biallelic frameshift/null variants presenting with temporal pole involvement on neuroimaging, indicating that the radiological boundary between recessive LoF and cysteine-altering missense variants is not categorical.

evidence.text: A systematic international cohort of 50 individuals with biallelic NOTCH3 variants confirmed a marked genotype-phenotype divergence: biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) caused a pediatric neurodevelopmental syndrome with spasticity and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) produced a classic CADASIL spectrum phenotype with adult-onset strokes, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without volume loss.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: A proband with a homozygous NOTCH3 null variant (c.2984delC) presented with livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions, distinguishing this recessive loss-of-function entity from CADASIL.

evidence.text: A 12-year-old consanguineous patient with a homozygous frameshift loss-of-function variant in NOTCH3 (c.2985_2991del) exhibited developmental delay, spastic tetraparesis, epilepsy, and leukodystrophy with white matter involvement extending into temporal regions, demonstrating that loss-of-function variants can exhibit atypical imaging overlapping with temporal pole pathology.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: We report a 12-year-old Moroccan girl, born to first-degree consanguineous parents, presenting with global developmental delay, spastic tetraparesis, epilepsy, and bilateral periventricular white matter abnormalities. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous frameshift variant in NOTCH3 (NM_000435.3:c.2985_2991del; NP_000426.2:p.(Gln996ArgfsTer274))

evidence.text: A compound heterozygous patient with two canonical cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variants demonstrated severe early onset of stroke, migraine, and progressive white matter changes characteristic of classical CADASIL pathology, confirming that biallelic cysteine-involving variants reproduce the classic CADASIL neuroradiological distribution.

source.title: The Spectrum of NOTCH3 Variants in an Australian CADASIL Cohort
source.quote: We also report the first CADASIL patient who is a compound heterozygote for two known pathogenic cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variants, who presented with a severe early onset of stroke, migraine, and white matter changes.

evidence.text: Analysis of 446 CADASIL patients shows that phenotypic severity and the distribution of ischemic tissue damage are heavily influenced by the specific location of the variant across EGFr domains in addition to vascular risk factors, demonstrating that even within cysteine-altering variants, imaging lesions show significant topographic variation.

source.title: Phenotypic variability in 446 CADASIL patients: impact of NOTCH3 gene mutation location in addition to the effects of age, sex and vascular risk factors
source.quote: The results confirmed that the mutation location is strongly related to clinical severity and showed that this effect is mainly driven by a different development of the most damaging ischemic tissue lesions at cerebral level.

conflicts: Iruzubieta et al. (2024) and Tasharrofi et al. (2024) establish a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome for biallelic loss-of-function variants characterized by periventricular/periatrial volume loss and absence of temporal pole hyperintensity, whereas Ouskri et al. (2025) report temporal white matter involvement in a patient with a homozygous frameshift/loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant.

The hypothesis assumes an invariant dichotomy ('strictly dictated') based purely on variant class (LoF vs cysteine missense), but emerging homozygous frameshift and cysteine-sparing variants exhibit variable penetrance and spatial distribution in white matter changes depending on genetic background, age, and disease duration.

new_directions.question_text: Does MRI re-review with standardized volumetric scoring confirm strict anterior temporal pole sparing in all published biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function cases versus cysteine-altering cases?
new_directions.rationale: Published case reports use varying descriptions (periventricular vs deep white matter vs temporal pole); a blinded central neuroradiological re-analysis of all known biallelic cases would definitively test whether anterior temporal pole sparing is pathognomonic.

new_directions.question_text: Do downstream transcriptomic profiles in human iPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle cells differ qualitatively between NOTCH3 null/frameshift variants and cysteine-altering missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether the distinct MRI patterns arise from pure loss of NOTCH3 signaling versus toxic aggregate deposition/GOM formation will establish the biochemical mechanism underlying temporal pole selectivity.
